svg.text: TOKEIRA · ARCHITECTURE
Deployments & versioning
Worker versions live in the delivery key, never in workflow semantics — a version decides where work routes, not what it means.
THE VOCABULARY
Versioning is a key dimension
QueueKey { namespace · task queue · kind ·
deployment · build_id }
A worker deployment (name + build) extends every queue
it polls. Two builds of one queue are two queues — no
flag on the task, no branch in the workflow, just routing.
unversioned workers use the bare key — versioning is
opt-in per queue, not a mode switch
WHO REMEMBERS WHAT
Edge — the operator surface
The WorkerDeployment RPC family (~20 surfaces): describe,
list, set current/ramping — Temporal's versioning grammar.
Runtime — the live view
The deployment registry plus version-membership and
reactivation caches — hot answers for routing decisions.
Storage — the record
worker_deployments · worker_deployment_token_seq
Durable deployment state behind WorkerDeploymentRepository.
THE THREE BEHAVIOURS
Polling registers
Every versioned poll registers its deployment as it arrives —
the system learns the fleet's builds from the fleet itself.
Transitions re-key
When a queue's current version changes, unversioned backlog
is promoted into the new version's queue — or absorbed back —
so waiting work follows the rollout instead of stranding.
Sticky respects rollouts
Sticky delivery re-routes when a deployment changes beneath
it — a workflow's affinity never pins it to a retired build.
A rollout, in one line of key changes
before: orders / checkout / wft / payments-svc / build-41 ← current
rollout: orders / checkout / wft / payments-svc / build-42 ← workers polling build-42 register it
cutover: current → build-42 · unversioned backlog promoted · sticky re-routes · build-41 drains its last tasks
No workflow noticed. History carries no build number in its semantics — the version only ever decided which workers were offered the work.
A caveat this corner has earned: upstream's worker-versioning surface was itself mid-evolution at the pin — the vendored protos carry in-place
deprecations pointing at successor fields. Tokeira implements the pinned shape; the compatibility matrix tracks verification, and this is the
corner most likely to move when the pins next advance.
The principle:
deployments are a delivery concern wearing an operator API — the commit path, the kernel, and history never learn what a build id is.
Companions: the delivery plane (the key in action) · the compatibility edge (where the RPC family is served).
